publications.explanation: C, non-verbal communication skills, is the intended answer. Gestures, eye contact, posture and personal distance can be interpreted differently across cultures, so a signal meant as respectful in one setting may be misunderstood in another. Attend to the person's context rather than assuming a gesture has one universal meaning. This does not mean culture is irrelevant to empathy, listening or persuasion; the question highlights the cultural interpretation of non-verbal signals. [CBSE, Non-verbal communication across cultures](https://cbseacademic.nic.in/web_material/Curriculum20/publication/srsec/employability-XI.pdf).

publications.paper_id: Old_Questions/Direct_2023-2025/MCS Combined 2023 Preliminary Exam Paper-I Series 'B'..pdf
publications.explanation:
D, 6.5°C per 1,000 metres, is the standard tropospheric lapse rate intended here. Equivalently, temperature falls by about 0.65°C per 100 metres. For example, a 2 km height increase corresponds to a 13°C decrease in this model.

This is a standard-atmosphere approximation, not a fixed rule for every place, weather condition or atmospheric layer. Actual temperature profiles vary and can include inversions. It also differs from the dry adiabatic rate of about 9.8°C/km for an unsaturated rising air parcel. [FAA, Aviation Weather, Table 1-2](https://www.faa.gov/documentLibrary/media/Advisory_Circular/AC_00-6B.pdf); [National Weather Service glossary](https://marine.weather.gov/glossary.php?word=lapse+rate).

publications.paper_id: Old_Questions/Direct_2023-2025/MCS Combined 2023 Preliminary Exam Paper-I Series 'D'.pdf
publications.explanation: B, biological treatment. Wastewater passes over a supporting medium coated with a film of microorganisms. These organisms break down organic matter, making a trickling filter an attached-growth biological process. The name “filter” can mislead: the principal treatment action is microbial degradation, rather than simply straining solids mechanically. Biological growth that detaches from the medium is subsequently removed in a clarifier. [EPA, Wastewater Technology Fact Sheet: Trickling Filters](https://www.epa.gov/system/files/documents/2022-10/trickling-filters-factsheet.pdf).
